raw_response:
I've been farming this land for over forty years. My father farmed it before me, and his father before him. I know this soil.

**My reasoning:**

Here in Quzhou, everyone grows wheat and maize. That is what we do. The soil is good for it, the water is there from the well, and the grain station buys it. I do not grow cotton anymore — prices fell and my back cannot handle the picking. I am 65. My son helps when he can, but he works in the city most of the year.

I have about 16 mu. I will plant all of it in winter wheat starting in October, then come June after the harvest I plant maize in the same fields. This is the rotation I have done my whole life. Last year my wheat was decent — around 440 jin per mu. I will try to do the same or a little better.

For wheat I will use the Jimai variety the seed shop recommends. It does well here. For maize I use hybrid seed — everyone uses Xianyu or Zhengdan now. The old varieties do not yield as well.

Fertilizer: I apply what my neighbor applies, maybe a little more. I was told I should use less nitrogen but I worry my yield will drop, so I keep it the same. I put down the base fertilizer before planting and top-dress during jointing stage.

Irrigation: wheat needs four waterings — before sowing, over winter, at jointing, and at heading. Maize needs one or two depending on rain. The pump is old but still works.

I spray herbicide early on and watch for aphids in wheat and corn borer in maize. Two or three sprays a season is normal.

I use a rotary tiller for wheat ground preparation. For maize I just go straight into the stubble — saves time and fuel.
